He signed a four-year contract with a €30 million release clause.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-41) Porto later re-sold 10% economic rights to third parties.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-42) On 18 July, he played his first game and scored his first goal in a friendly against [Ajax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Ajax "AFC Ajax").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-43) In November, Porto sold 35% economic rights (half of 70%) to Gol Football Luxembourg, S.A.R.L. for €2.5 million.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-44)

On 15 December 2010, Rodríguez scored his first competitive goal during a 3–1 [Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_UEFA_Europa_League "2010–11 UEFA Europa League") home victory against Bulgarian club [CSKA Sofia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PFC_CSKA_Sofia "PFC CSKA Sofia").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-45) On 17 May, Porto bought the remaining 30% economic rights from Convergence Capital Partners B.V. for €2.25 million and once again hold more than half of the economic rights with 55%.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-46) He scored a hat-trick and assisted once against [Vitória de Guimarães](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vit%C3%B3ria_de_Guimar%C3%A3es "Vitória de Guimarães") in the [2011 Taça de Portugal Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Ta%C3%A7a_de_Portugal_Final "2011 Taça de Portugal Final"), which Porto won 6–2.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-:1-48)

On 13 June, Rodríguez signed a new five-year contract in which the release clause increased to €45 million.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-49) He finished the [2010–11 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_FC_Porto_season "2010–11 FC Porto season") with six goals and eight assists in 31 appearances. He also took home four trophies: the [Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Superta%C3%A7a_C%C3%A2ndido_de_Oliveira "2010 Supertaça Cândido de Oliveira") title, the [league title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Primeira_Liga "2010–11 Primeira Liga"), the [Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_UEFA_Europa_League "2010–11 UEFA Europa League") title, and the [Cup title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Ta%C3%A7a_de_Portugal "2010–11 Taça de Portugal") as Porto had a historic season.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-Soccerway_profile-50)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-:1-48)

#### 2011–12 season

In the [2011–12 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_FC_Porto_season "2011–12 FC Porto season"), Rodríguez scored 14 goals for Porto and delivered 11 assists. In 2011, he won the [LPFP Award for Breakthrough Player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LPFP_Awards "LPFP Awards") of [2011–12 Primeira Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Primeira_Liga "2011–12 Primeira Liga") season at age 20, becoming the first Colombian player to do so. He is a two-time winner of the [SJPF Player of the Month](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SJPF_Player_of_the_Month "SJPF Player of the Month"). He won the [Portuguese Golden Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_Golden_Ball "Portuguese Golden Ball") award in 2012, becoming the second Colombian to win the award after [Radamel Falcao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radamel_Falcao "Radamel Falcao") as well as the youngest player ever to hold the honour.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-51)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-bleacherreport-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-53) On 20 September 2011 in a league match against [Feirense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C.D._Feirense "C.D. Feirense"), he punched [Rabiola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabiola "Rabiola") and was subsequently dismissed, missing [the match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/O_Cl%C3%A1ssico "O Clássico") against [Benfica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.L._Benfica "S.L. Benfica").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-54)

#### 2012–13 season

In the [2012–13 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_FC_Porto_season "2012–13 FC Porto season"), Rodríguez was given the number 10 shirt and became a regular starter. Since fellow Colombians [Radamel Falcao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radamel_Falcao "Radamel Falcao"), [Fredy Guarín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fredy_Guar%C3%ADn "Fredy Guarín") and Brazilian [Hulk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hulk_(footballer) "Hulk (footballer)") left the club during the last two seasons, Rodríguez was able to start more regularly than before. In a match against [Olhanense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.C._Olhanense "S.C. Olhanense") on 1 September, he scored a chip from a tight angle. In the same game, he assisted compatriot [Jackson Martínez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Mart%C3%ADnez "Jackson Martínez") with a through ball for an eventual 3–2 win. He scored the team's third goal against [Beira-Mar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.C._Beira-Mar "S.C. Beira-Mar") soon after assisting the first two goals in a 4–0 victory on 22 September.

In the [2012–13 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_UEFA_Champions_League "2012–13 UEFA Champions League") group stage, he scored against French club [Paris Saint-Germain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_F.C. "Paris Saint-Germain F.C.") in a 1–0 victory, allowing Porto to top their current group.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-55) A few days later, Rodríguez scored a penalty against rivals [Sporting CP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporting_Clube_de_Portugal "Sporting Clube de Portugal"). Because of his great start to the 2012–13 season, he won the [SJPF Player of the Month](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SJPF_Player_of_the_Month "SJPF Player of the Month") award for August/September.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-58) In the Champions League against [Dinamo Kyiv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Dynamo_Kyiv "FC Dynamo Kyiv") on 24 October, he assisted Jackson Martínez to an eventual 3–2 home victory.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-59) He scored Porto's last two goals in a 5–0 win over [Marítimo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C.S._Mar%C3%ADtimo "C.S. Marítimo") on 2 November.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-60) In the 90th minute against [Braga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.C._Braga "S.C. Braga"), Rodríguez scored a goal in an eventual 2–0 away victory.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-61)

Prior to the second half of the season, he suffered a hamstring injury causing him to struggle to maintain fitness. In a match against [Nacional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C.D._Nacional "C.D. Nacional") on 5 January, he injured his hamstring once more and was subsequently substituted after the first half. The injury sidelined him for a month.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-62)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-63) On 1 February 2013, Porto bought back 35% economic rights of Rodríguez from Gol Football Luxembourg for €8.75 million[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-64) (by selling 47.5% economic rights of [Diego Reyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Antonio_Reyes "Diego Antonio Reyes") for €3.5 million[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-65)), which Porto sold in November 2010 for €2.5 million.

Rodríguez made his return at the 70th minute in the 2–0 victory over Beira-Mar on 23 February, his first match since being injured for more than a month. In his second league match since his return, he assisted a goal against Rio Ave with a wonderful cross. On 8 March, he assisted a goal against [Estoril](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G.D._Estoril_Praia "G.D. Estoril Praia") from a corner in a 2–0 victory.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-66) It was Rodríguez' first start in two months.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-67) He did not start in the second leg of the Champions League match against Málaga until the second half when Porto was down to ten men after the dismiss of a defender. Porto lost the match and coach [Vítor Pereira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V%C3%ADtor_Pereira_(footballer,_born_1968) "Vítor Pereira (footballer, born 1968)") was greatly criticized and questioned why Rodríguez did not start sooner, considering that the player was a key member and Porto could have had a more solid team. Rodríguez expressed his disappointment, claiming to be "100%" in good health (as well as giving a performance with no struggles shown). However, he also expressed his respect and understanding to the coach's concern.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-70) Despite an exit from the Champions League, Rodríguez went on to become the second-most fouled player in the tournament that year.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-71)

[Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") reportedly made a bid for €30 million to purchase Rodríguez, though Porto rejected the offer as being too low.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-73) He scored his first [Taça da Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ta%C3%A7a_da_Liga "Taça da Liga") goal, a penalty, in the [2012–13 Taça da Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_Ta%C3%A7a_da_Liga "2012–13 Taça da Liga") semi-final against Rio Ave. Porto won the match 4–0 and advanced to the final. In the final on 13 April, Porto lost 1–0 to Braga, with Rodríguez playing 75 minutes. Five days before the final, he gave a man of the match performance against Braga, scoring the first goal and assisting two in a 3–1 victory.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In the final match of the season against [Paços de Ferreira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F.C._Pa%C3%A7os_de_Ferreira "F.C. Paços de Ferreira") on 19 May, Rodríguez was tripped inside the box and secured a penalty that was later scored by Lucho Gonzalez, which contributed to the 2–0 victory that led to Porto's third consecutive league title.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-74)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-75) In all competitions that season, he scored 13 goals and provided 15 assists in 32 appearances. Winning the league title meant that Rodríguez, at 21, won his eighth trophy since joining the club three years prior.

### Monaco

On 25 May 2013, it was announced that Rodríguez had joined [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Monaco_FC "AS Monaco FC") for a transfer fee of €45 million, [the second most expensive transfer in Portuguese football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_expensive_association_football_transfers "List of most expensive association football transfers") behind former teammate [Hulk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hulk_(footballer) "Hulk (footballer)"). Rodríguez subsequently signed a five-year contract that was set to keep him at the club until 2018.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-76) This transfer made him not only one of the most expensive transfers in the club's history, but in [Ligue 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ligue_1 "Ligue 1") history as well, along as one of the highest in world football.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-bleacherreport.com-77) Rodríguez made his Monaco debut against [Bordeaux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Girondins_de_Bordeaux "FC Girondins de Bordeaux"), a game Monaco went on to win 2–0. He then missed Monaco's second league match to avoid a possible injury.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-78) On 5 October against [Saint-Étienne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Saint-%C3%89tienne "AS Saint-Étienne"), Rodríguez gave a man of the match performance by assisting both goals in a 2–1 victory.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-79)

He finally scored his first goal for the club with a free-kick in a 2–0 win over [Rennes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_Rennais_F.C. "Stade Rennais F.C.").[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-comutricolor2-80) Rodríguez scored another goal in the next match in the fourth minute against [Nice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OGC_Nice "OGC Nice"), a game Monaco won 3–0.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-81) He began the 2014 calendar year by making his [Coupe de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coupe_de_France "Coupe de France") debut in a match against [Vannes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vannes_OC "Vannes OC"), where he both assisted and scored a goal in a 3–2 victory.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-sportsmole-82) His first double at Monaco came in the match against [Bastia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SC_Bastia "SC Bastia"), a 2–0 Monaco victory.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-yahoo-83)

In the French media, Rodríguez was referred to as "perhaps" the best footballer in Ligue 1 due to his impressive debut season with Monaco,[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-nicematin-84) although he stated that he still required more time in the league to fully adapt.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-onzemondial-85) Following the international break, he scored his first penalty for Monaco against Sochaux in a 2–1 win.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-fifa2-86) He ended his debut season without a trophy, though nonetheless helped Monaco secure a spot in the following season's [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League"). On an individual level, he earned a spot in the star [Ligue 1 XI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troph%C3%A9es_UNFP_du_football "Trophées UNFP du football"),[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-mundodeportivo.com-87) and led Ligue 1 in assists for the season.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-espnfc.com-88)

### Real Madrid

> "I've always followed Real Madrid and always dreamed of playing here [...] I will never forget this day [...] I know I am under a lot of pressure, but I am happy to face it."

—Rodríguez on his move to Real Madrid[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-89)

In a post-match interview during the [2014 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup "2014 FIFA World Cup"), Rodríguez stated his "love", "admiration" and "passion" for [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_C.F. "Real Madrid C.F."), saying that it would be a "life's dream" to play for them after his performances aroused rumors linking him to the Spanish club.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-90)

On 22 July 2014, Rodríguez signed a six-year contract with the Spanish club for an undisclosed fee, which was reported to be approximately €80 million.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-91)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-92)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-93) At the time, this was the [fourth-most expensive transfer in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_expensive_association_football_transfers "List of most expensive association football transfers"), the third-most expensive in Madrid's history, and the most expensive Colombian after surpassing [Radamel Falcao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radamel_Falcao "Radamel Falcao")'s €60 million transfer in 2013.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-94)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-95) The amount spent on his transfer fee led many to call Rodríguez as a _[Galáctico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gal%C3%A1cticos "Galácticos")_ after he was given the number 10 shirt worn by Madrid legends such as [Luís Figo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lu%C3%ADs_Figo "Luís Figo") and [Ferenc Puskás](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferenc_Pusk%C3%A1s "Ferenc Puskás").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-96)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-97)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-98)

Rodríguez was greeted by a 45,000 attendance during his presentation. The Colombian ambassador in [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid "Madrid") made a speech at the event and carried a message from Colombian President [Juan Manuel Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Manuel_Santos "Juan Manuel Santos") that Rodríguez was changing the history of Colombian football and that the entire nation was behind him.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-youtube.com-99) Real Madrid President [Florentino Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florentino_P%C3%A9rez "Florentino Pérez") followed with a speech of his own, stating that he welcomed Rodríguez, a "lover" and "long supporter" of the club who would never forget the day he made his dream a reality.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-100)

#### 2014–17: Debut season success, La Liga and UEFA Champions League titles

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/76/James_Rodriguez_-_panoramio.jpg/250px-James_Rodriguez_-_panoramio.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:James_Rodriguez_-_panoramio.jpg)

Rodríguez during his presentation as a [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") ahead of the [2014–15 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Real_Madrid_CF_season "2014–15 Real Madrid CF season")

Rodríguez made his debut in the [UEFA Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_UEFA_Super_Cup "2014 UEFA Super Cup") at the [Cardiff City Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_City_Stadium "Cardiff City Stadium") against [Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC"), in which Real Madrid won 2–0. He played 72 minutes before being replaced by [Isco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isco "Isco").[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-101) On 19 August, Rodríguez scored his first goal for Real Madrid against [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid") in the first leg of the [Spanish Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Supercopa_de_Espa%C3%B1a "2014 Supercopa de España") after coming on as a substitute for [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo "Cristiano Ronaldo") at half-time.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-102) Rodríguez made his Champions League debut for Real in the group stage opening match against [Basel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Basel "FC Basel"), where he scored the fourth goal in a 5–1 victory.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-103) He then scored his first league goal days later against [Deportivo La Coruña](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deportivo_de_La_Coru%C3%B1a "Deportivo de La Coruña"), where he also supplied an assist in an 8–2 victory.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-104) He scored a brace in a 4–0 win at [Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granada_CF "Granada CF") on 1 November; his first goal was a dipping volley from a poor angle.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-105)

In the match against Sevilla in which he scored the opening goal, Rodríguez experienced a [fracture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone_fracture "Bone fracture") on the [fifth metatarsal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_metatarsal "Fifth metatarsal") in his right foot after being fouled. The injury required surgery and he was out of action for two months.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-106) He returned on 5 April in the match against Granada, where he assisted two goals in a 9–1 victory before being subbed at the 60th minute.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-107)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-108) Days later, he scored his first goal since his injury against [Rayo Vallecano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rayo_Vallecano "Rayo Vallecano") in a 2–0 victory.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-109)

After being left on the bench for his team's season opener, a scoreless draw against [Sporting Gijón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporting_Gij%C3%B3n "Sporting Gijón"), Rodríguez made his first contribution of the season by giving a man of the match performance against [Real Betis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis "Real Betis"). The player scored with both a spectacular free-kick and [bicycle kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_kick "Bicycle kick") and provided an assist for [Gareth Bale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gareth_Bale "Gareth Bale").[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-110) On 8 September 2015, during an international friendly match against Peru, he collided with Peruvian player [Juan Manuel Vargas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Manuel_Vargas "Juan Manuel Vargas"),[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-111) and though he initially appeared able to continue, Rodríguez was removed from the game as a precautionary measure.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-112) He was diagnosed with a thigh muscle tear,[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-113) and didn't return to training until 27 October.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-114) He played his first match since the injury on 8 November, scoring in a 3–2 loss to Sevilla.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-115) On 31 January 2016, he scored and assisted [Karim Benzema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karim_Benzema "Karim Benzema")'s goal in a 6–0 thrashing of [Espanyol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCD_Espanyol "RCD Espanyol").[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-116) On 8 March, he scored his first and only goal of the [2015–16 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_UEFA_Champions_League "2015–16 UEFA Champions League"), in a 2–0 victory against [Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.S._Roma "A.S. Roma") to help his club get into the quarter-finals.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-117) His team eventually won the Champions League, with Rodríguez making five appearances.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-118)

Rodríguez made 22 appearances when Madrid won the [2016–17 La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_La_Liga "2016–17 La Liga"),[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-119)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-120) and six when Madrid won the [2016–17 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_UEFA_Champions_League "2016–17 UEFA Champions League").[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-121) Despite scoring 11 goals, (including braces against Granada,[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-122) Deportivo,[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-123) and Sevilla[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-124)), as well as providing 13 assists, he failed to gain more playing time under Zidane even with his influence on the pitch, leading him to request a loan transfer for more playing time.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-125)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-bundesliga.com-126)

#### 2017–19: Loan to Bayern Munich

> "He has the ability to see the hole where others cannot find it. This has already been shown in several games this season. His vision of the game is reminiscent of what [Michael Laudrup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Laudrup "Michael Laudrup") had and the great beneficiaries are his teammates."

—_[Marca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marca\_(newspaper) "Marca (newspaper)")_ writer Justin Sherman, regarding Rodríguez' first season with Bayern[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-marca.com-127)

On 11 July 2017, it was announced that Rodríguez had been loaned to [Bayern Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Bayern_Munich "FC Bayern Munich") on a two-year long deal.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-128)[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-129) Bayern paid Real Madrid €13 million as a loan fee for the two season-long loan. With his loan deal to Bayern, he reunited with his old Madrid manager [Carlo Ancelotti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlo_Ancelotti "Carlo Ancelotti"). Bayern had the option to buy Rodríguez for €42 million at the end of the loan period.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-130) He scored his first goal of his loan spell in a 3–0 away win over [Schalke 04](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schalke_04 "Schalke 04").[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-131) After a slow start to his Bayern career, mainly due to an injury in preseason, Rodríguez rediscovered his form after [Jupp Heynckes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jupp_Heynckes "Jupp Heynckes") was hired as Bayern's manager in October as the club sacked Ancelotti.

On 2 April 2018, Bayern's CEO, [Karl-Heinz Rummenigge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Heinz_Rummenigge "Karl-Heinz Rummenigge"), thanked Ancelotti for bringing Rodríguez to Bayern. "It was a very, very good transfer and I have to thank Carlo Ancelotti once again," Rummenigge said.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-132)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/2019-03-09_Fu%C3%9Fball%2C_M%C3%A4nner%2C_1._Bundesliga%2C_FC_Bayern_M%C3%BCnchen_-_VfL_Wolfsburg_StP_2655_by_Stepro.jpg/250px-2019-03-09_Fu%C3%9Fball%2C_M%C3%A4nner%2C_1._Bundesliga%2C_FC_Bayern_M%C3%BCnchen_-_VfL_Wolfsburg_StP_2655_by_Stepro.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2019-03-09_Fu%C3%9Fball,_M%C3%A4nner,_1._Bundesliga,_FC_Bayern_M%C3%BCnchen_-_VfL_Wolfsburg_StP_2655_by_Stepro.jpg)

Rodríguez playing for [Bayern Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Bayern_Munich "FC Bayern Munich") against [Wolfsburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VfL_Wolfsburg "VfL Wolfsburg") in March 2019

In the semi-finals of the [2017–18 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_UEFA_Champions_League "2017–18 UEFA Champions League") season, Rodríguez scored the equalizing goal in a 2–2 draw against his parent club at the [Santiago Bernabéu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_Stadium "Santiago Bernabéu Stadium"), but Bayern failed to reach the final as they lost 3–4 on aggregate.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-133) However, Rodríguez went on to win the [2017–18 Bundesliga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_Bundesliga "2017–18 Bundesliga") title with Bayern, credited as a key member behind their title defense for his contribution of 7 goals and 11 assists in 23 Bundesliga appearances.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-bundesliga.com-126)[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-2017%E2%80%9318_season-134)

On 15 September 2018, Rodríguez scored his opening goal of the [season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_FC_Bayern_Munich_season "2018–19 FC Bayern Munich season") in a 3–1 victory over [Bayer Leverkusen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayer_04_Leverkusen "Bayer 04 Leverkusen").[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-135) On 17 March 2019, he scored three goals in a 6–0 league win over [Mainz 05](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1._FSV_Mainz_05 "1. FSV Mainz 05"), his first hat-trick since 2011, with Porto.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-136) On 18 May, he won his second Bundesliga title as Bayern finished two points above [Dortmund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borussia_Dortmund "Borussia Dortmund") with 78 points. A week later, he won his first [DFB-Pokal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DFB-Pokal "DFB-Pokal") as Bayern defeated [RB Leipzig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RB_Leipzig "RB Leipzig") 3–0 in the [2019 DFB-Pokal Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_DFB-Pokal_Final "2019 DFB-Pokal Final"). Rodríguez did not appear in the match as he was out injured.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-137) He appeared in 28 matches and scored seven goals in all competitions. On 5 June, it was announced that Bayern Munich would not pick up the buy option and he would return to Real Madrid.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-138)

#### 2019–20: Final season and departure

After his return to Madrid, Rodríguez made eight appearances during the league season, as Real Madrid won the [2019–20 La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_La_Liga "2019–20 La Liga").[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-139)

### Everton

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/Manchester_United_v_Everton%2C_7_August_2021_%2811%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Manchester_United_v_Everton%2C_7_August_2021_%2811%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Manchester_United_v_Everton,_7_August_2021_(11)_(cropped).jpg)

Rodríguez during a [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League") match against [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") in August 2021

On 7 September 2020, Rodríguez joined [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League") club [Everton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everton_F.C. "Everton F.C.") on a free transfer and signed a two-year deal, with a club option for a third season.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-:0-140)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-141) The deal once again reunited him with manager Carlo Ancelotti.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-142) He made his debut later that month in a 1–0 away win against [Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C.") in their first game of the [2020–21 Premier League season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020%E2%80%9321_Premier_League "2020–21 Premier League").[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-143) The following week he scored his first goal for Everton on his home debut, a 5–2 league win against [West Bromwich Albion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bromwich_Albion_F.C. "West Bromwich Albion F.C.").[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-144) He scored two goals and provided an assist for his international teammate [Yerry Mina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yerry_Mina "Yerry Mina") in a 4–2 victory at Goodison Park against [Brighton & Hove Albion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brighton_&_Hove_Albion_F.C. "Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.") on 3 October 2020.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-145) He added to his goal tally against [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") in a 3–3 draw at [Old Trafford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Trafford "Old Trafford") on 6 February 2021.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-146)

### Al-Rayyan

On 22 September 2021, Rodríguez joined [Al-Rayyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Rayyan_SC "Al-Rayyan SC") for an undisclosed fee.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-147)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-148) On 17 October 2021, Rodríguez made his debut for Al-Rayyan, in a 3–0 loss against [Al-Duhail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Duhail_SC "Al-Duhail SC").[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-149) He scored his first goal for the team against [Al-Sailiya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Sailiya_SC "Al-Sailiya SC") on 26 October 2021.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-150) On 15 September 2022, Al-Rayyan and the player parted ways.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-151)

### Olympiacos

On 15 September 2022, Rodríguez joined [Greek Super League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_League_Greece "Super League Greece") champions [Olympiacos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympiacos_F.C. "Olympiacos F.C.") on a free transfer.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-152) Upon arrival, Rodríguez was handed the number 10 jersey, previously worn by [Rony Lopes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rony_Lopes "Rony Lopes") who had departed to play on loan for Ligue 1 side [Troyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ES_Troyes_AC "ES Troyes AC").[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-153) He made his league debut on 18 September as a starter against [Aris Thessaloniki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aris_Thessaloniki "Aris Thessaloniki"), a match in which his team lost 2–1 despite being up a goal for the majority of the match.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-154) On 13 April 2023, Rodríguez' contract with Olympiacos was terminated by mutual consent.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-155)

### São Paulo

On 29 July 2023, Rodríguez joined [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC "São Paulo FC"), signing a two-year contract.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-156) He made his debut for the club in a 1–1 draw with Flamengo on 13 August. Despite making mostly substitute appearances as he was coming from four months off the pitch, he was getting regular playing time under manager [Dorival Júnior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorival_J%C3%BAnior "Dorival Júnior") in the 2023 season, making 14 appearances out of a possible 25 until an injury suffered in training left him out for the final three matches of the season.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-157)[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-158) However, with the arrival of [Luis Zubeldía](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Zubeld%C3%ADa "Luis Zubeldía"), Rodríguez began struggling for playing time, playing less than 200 minutes over 8 appearances in the first half of the 2024 season, with coach Zubeldia preferring other players in his position instead.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-159) In July 2024 his contract with São Paulo was terminated by mutual consent, with Rodríguez making 22 appearances and scoring two goals in his spell with the Brazilian club.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-160)

### Rayo Vallecano

Rodríguez joined [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga") club [Rayo Vallecano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rayo_Vallecano "Rayo Vallecano") in August 2024 as a free agent.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-161) He made a total of seven appearances in the 2024–25 season for a total of 205 minutes and provided an [assist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assist_(association_football) "Assist (association football)") in Rayo's Copa del Rey victory over [Unionistas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unionistas_de_Salamanca_CF "Unionistas de Salamanca CF"). His contract with Rayo was terminated by mutual consent in January 2025 after only four months and seven appearances with the club.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-162)

### León

Following his departure from Rayo, there was speculation about a transfer to [Junior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atletico_Junior "Atletico Junior"),[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-163) with club president Fuad Char saying that he would be paid one of the biggest salaries in Colombian football.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-164) On 13 January 2025, [Liga MX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liga_MX "Liga MX") club [León](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Le%C3%B3n "Club León") announced Rodríguez' signing following his departure from Rayo.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-165)[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-166) On 26 January, he netted his first goal from a penalty in a 1–0 victory over [Juárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Ju%C3%A1rez "FC Juárez").[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-167) However, his contract with the club was not renewed and would become a free agent at the end of the same year.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-168)

### Minnesota United

On 6 February 2026, Rodríguez signed with [Major League Soccer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Soccer "Major League Soccer") club [Minnesota United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_United_FC "Minnesota United FC") on a deal through to June 2026, with a club option through to December 2026.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-169) On 13 May 2026, Minnesota United announced Rodríguez would depart the club to prepare for the [2026 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup "2026 FIFA World Cup").[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-170)

### Atlético Nacional

On 12 September 2026, Rodríguez joined [Atlético Nacional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Nacional "Atlético Nacional"), marking his return to Colombian football.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-171)

## International career

### Youth

Rodríguez was part of the [Colombia U-17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia_national_under-17_football_team "Colombia national under-17 football team") team that finished runners-up in the [2007 South American Under-17 Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_South_American_Under-17_Football_Championship "2007 South American Under-17 Football Championship"), where he scored three goals. He also helped Colombia advance to the knockout stages during the [2007 FIFA U-17 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_FIFA_U-17_World_Cup "2007 FIFA U-17 World Cup"), where they eventually lost to the winners of the tournament [Nigeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_under-17_football_team "Nigeria national under-17 football team").[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-:2-172) He was also part of the [Colombia under-20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia_national_under-20_football_team "Colombia national under-20 football team") squad in three youth tournaments during 2011: the [Toulon Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toulon_Tournament "Toulon Tournament"), the [South American U-20 Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_South_American_U-20_Championship "2011 South American U-20 Championship") and the [U-20 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_FIFA_U-20_World_Cup "2011 FIFA U-20 World Cup") that was held in his homeland Colombia. Rodríguez scored two goals and provided three assists during the [2011 Toulon Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Toulon_Tournament "2011 Toulon Tournament"). This show led him to being voted as the [MVP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Most_valuable_player "Most valuable player") of the tournament where Colombia won the final by defeating [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_national_under-20_football_team "France national under-20 football team") in a [penalty shootout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)"). Rodríguez scored one of the penalties in the shootout.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-173)

During the [2011 South American U-20 Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_South_American_U-20_Championship "2011 South American U-20 Championship"), he provided three assists. During the [2011 U-20 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_FIFA_U-20_World_Cup "2011 FIFA U-20 World Cup"), he was named [captain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_(association_football) "Captain (association football)") of the U20 squad due to his impressive leadership and talent. By scoring three goals and providing three assists in the tournament, he gained international attention as a promising star, especially during his performance in the 4–1 victory against France where he scored a penalty and provided an assist.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-174)[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-:2-172)

### Senior

#### 2014 World Cup qualification and friendlies

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Polic%C3%ADa_de_Infancia_y_Adolescencia_-_James_Rodr%C3%ADguez_%28cropped%29.jpeg/250px-Polic%C3%ADa_de_Infancia_y_Adolescencia_-_James_Rodr%C3%ADguez_%28cropped%29.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Polic%C3%ADa_de_Infancia_y_Adolescencia_-_James_Rodr%C3%ADguez_(cropped).jpeg)

Rodríguez with [Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia_national_football_team "Colombia national football team") in March 2013

On 29 September 2011, Rodríguez received his first call-up to the [Colombia senior side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia_national_football_team "Colombia national football team") for a match against [Bolivia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolivia_national_football_team "Bolivia national football team") on 11 October 2011.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-175) He was selected as the man of match due to his performance, including the initiation of the goal scored in the last minute by his former Porto teammate [Radamel Falcao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radamel_Falcao "Radamel Falcao") which gave Colombia a 2–1 win in [La Paz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Paz "La Paz").[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-176) Under new manager [José Pékerman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_P%C3%A9kerman "José Pékerman"), he played a crucial part in setting up both goals in a 2–0 friendly victory over [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_national_football_team "Mexico national football team"). He scored his first goal for Colombia against [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru_national_football_team "Peru national football team"), and Colombia went on to win 1–0 in [Lima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lima "Lima") in Pekerman's first competitive match.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-177)

Rodríguez assisted two goals in a row from 1–0 to 3–0 In the [World Cup qualifying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_(CONMEBOL) "2014 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)") match against [Uruguay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uruguay_national_football_team "Uruguay national football team") that eventually ended 4–0. He scored a stunning [volley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volley_(football) "Volley (football)") from a 30-yard free kick against [Chile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chile_national_football_team "Chile national football team"), leveling the game to an eventual 3–1 away victory boosting Colombia to the second place in the qualifying stages. In the match against [Paraguay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paraguay_national_football_team "Paraguay national football team"), he set up the plays leading towards both goals in a 2–0 victory. In Colombia's last international friendly of the year, he assisted the sole goal, allowing Colombia to tie with [2014 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup "2014 FIFA World Cup") hosts [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team") 1–1. Rodríguez played his first match of 2013 in the second half of the [CONMEBOL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CONMEBOL "CONMEBOL") qualifiers against [Bolivia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolivia_national_football_team "Bolivia national football team"), where he gave a man of the match performance in a 5–0 victory. He set up the second goal thanks to a free kick that he took.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-178)

Playing against South American leaders [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina_national_football_team "Argentina national football team"), Rodríguez suffered an injury in the 30th minute forcing him to be substituted. While the injury was not serious, he was rested and therefore missed the game against Peru days later. He made a good comeback when he scored the winning goal in a 1–0 victory over [Ecuador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecuador_national_football_team "Ecuador national football team") during the final stages of the world cup qualifiers. In a tough match against Chile, he drew both penalties that equalized Colombia from a 1–3 to a 3–3. This drew allowed Colombia to return to the World Cup for the first time in 16 years. Days later, he assisted the first goal with a free-kick while setting up the second in a 2–1 away victory over Paraguay.

Rodríguez continued his play-making form by assisting the first goal and setting up the second against [Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium_national_football_team "Belgium national football team") in a 2–0 victory. He was later voted man of the match.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-179) A few days later, He was praised once more as the man of the match in a 0–0 draw against the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_national_football_team "Netherlands national football team").[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-yahoo2-180) Rodríguez started in Colombia's opening match of 2014 and scored a penalty against [Tunisia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tunisia_national_football_team "Tunisia national football team") in a 1–1 draw at [Estadio Cornellá-El Prat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estadio_Cornell%C3%A1-El_Prat "Estadio Cornellá-El Prat") on 5 March 2014.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-181) In the last friendly before the World Cup, he scored yet another penalty against [Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_national_football_team "Jordan national football team") in a 3–0 victory.

#### 2014 World Cup

> "For me, special talents are those who do things that are completely out of the ordinary. [Diego Maradona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Maradona "Diego Maradona"), [Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi"), [Luis Suárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Su%C3%A1rez "Luis Suárez"), James Rodriguez– they do things because they have certain gifts that make them special. I believe he's the best player at the World Cup and I don't think I'm exaggerating; he's a young player. We tried to limit his influence, but he kept going and made his presence felt. Hopefully he'll continue to progress, because he's very young. Football needs players with these characteristics."

—[Óscar Tabárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%93scar_Tab%C3%A1rez "Óscar Tabárez") on Rodríguez[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-182)

On 2 June 2014, Rodríguez was named in Colombia's 23-man squad for the [2014 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup "2014 FIFA World Cup") and assigned the number 10 shirt.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-183) In the team's opening match of the tournament, he set up the first two goals, scored a last-minute goal with a low shot to seal a 3–0 victory over [Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greece_national_football_team "Greece national football team") and was named man of the match by [FIFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA "FIFA").[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-184) In the second match, he continued his form by scoring with a header and setting up a second goal for [Juan Fernando Quintero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Fernando_Quintero "Juan Fernando Quintero") in a 2–1 victory over [Ivory Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivory_Coast_national_football_team "Ivory Coast national football team") and was once again elected as man of the match.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-185) In the final group stage match against [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan_national_football_team "Japan national football team"), Rodríguez came on as a second-half substitute and assisted two [Jackson Martínez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Mart%C3%ADnez "Jackson Martínez") goals before scoring the final goal in a 4–1 victory.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-186)[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-187) At the end of the group stage, he was ranked as the best performing player at the tournament by [FIFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA "FIFA").[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-188)

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/James_Rodriguez.jpg/250px-James_Rodriguez.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:James_Rodriguez.jpg)

Rodríguez celebrates after scoring a penalty against [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team") at the [2014 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup "2014 FIFA World Cup")

On 28 June, Rodríguez scored both goals to defeat [Uruguay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uruguay_national_football_team "Uruguay national football team") 2–0 at the [Maracanã](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Est%C3%A1dio_do_Maracan%C3%A3 "Estádio do Maracanã") in the [round of 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage "2014 FIFA World Cup knockout stage"), taking Colombia to its first ever World Cup [quarter-finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Quarter-finals "2014 FIFA World Cup knockout stage"). These goals made him the first player to score in all of his team's opening matches since [Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronaldo_(Brazilian_footballer) "Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)") and [Rivaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rivaldo "Rivaldo") in [2002](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_FIFA_World_Cup "2002 FIFA World Cup").[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-189) His volleyed opening goal was described as "one of the greatest goals the World Cup has ever seen" by opposing manager [Óscar Tabárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%93scar_Tab%C3%A1rez "Óscar Tabárez"), who also called Rodríguez "the best player in the World Cup".[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-190) Because of his performance against the Uruguayans, he was named by FIFA as man of the match for the third time in four matches.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-191) The volley was later voted as the best goal in the tournament by more than four million people on FIFA's website[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-WC14_Best_Goal-192) and won the [FIFA Puskás Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_Pusk%C3%A1s_Award "FIFA Puskás Award") for the best goal of the year.[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-193)[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-194) In the [quarter-final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Quarter-finals "2014 FIFA World Cup knockout stage") against Brazil, he scored his sixth goal of the tournament, a penalty in Colombia's 2–1 defeat.[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-195)

A tearful Rodríguez was consoled by Brazil's [David Luiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Luiz "David Luiz") and stated: "He (David) told me I was a good player. The truth is that having so many superstars hug me did make me happy. We have to raise our heads now and thank Colombia for their support. We are sad because we wanted to keep going and set new records. We gave everything to reach the semi-final, but we have to be proud because we played a great side. I'm crying because we gave everything. We're sad but we also have to feel proud because we left our skin out there."[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-196)[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-197) Luiz and Rodríguez also exchanged jerseys. Rodríguez received a standing ovation from the home crowd, ending his first World Cup campaign with six goals and two assists in five matches.[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-198) On 11 July, he was named on the ten-man shortlist for FIFA's [Golden Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup#Golden_Ball "2014 FIFA World Cup") award for the tournament's best player.[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-199) He then won the [Golden Boot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_Golden_Shoe "FIFA World Cup Golden Shoe") as the tournament's top goalscorer despite being eliminated in the quarter finals.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-fifa.com-200) Due to his performances, he was named in the [World Cup All Star XI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_Golden_Shoe#All-Star_Team "FIFA World Cup Golden Shoe") and was also listed in the Cup's star XI by [Castrol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castrol "Castrol")'s index rating system in FIFA's website.[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-ReferenceA-201) Argentina legend [Diego Maradona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Maradona "Diego Maradona") argued that Rodríguez, rather than [Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi"), should have won the tournament's [Golden Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adidas_Golden_Ball "Adidas Golden Ball") award.[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-202)

#### 2015 Copa América, Copa América Centenario, 2018 World Cup qualification and friendlies

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bf/James_Rodr%C3%ADguez_2016.jpg/250px-James_Rodr%C3%ADguez_2016.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:James_Rodr%C3%ADguez_2016.jpg)

Rodríguez before training in Chicago for the [Copa América Centenario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Am%C3%A9rica_Centenario "Copa América Centenario") in June 2016

Rodríguez was called up to represent Colombia at the [2015 Copa América](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Copa_Am%C3%A9rica "2015 Copa América") in Chile,[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-203) where his team was eliminated 5–4 on penalties by eventual finalists Argentina on 27 June, following a 0–0 draw.[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-204) The following summer, Rodríguez joined Colombia's squad for the [Copa América Centenario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Am%C3%A9rica_Centenario "Copa América Centenario") and was named the team's [captain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_(association_football) "Captain (association football)").[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-205) On 3 June, he started in Colombia's opening 2–0 win against tournament hosts the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_men's_national_soccer_team "United States men's national soccer team"), scoring his team's second goal from the penalty spot although he was forced off early due to an injury.[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-206) It was initially feared that he would be unable to feature in his nation's second group match against [Paraguay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paraguay_national_football_team "Paraguay national football team"),[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-207) but he recovered in time to start the match, setting up Colombia's first goal, and later scoring one himself in a 2–1 win which sealed his team a place in the quarter-finals of the tournament.[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-208) Colombia would then lose in the semi-finals against eventual and defending champions Chile, before securing a third-place victory against the host nation for Colombia's best result since 2001.[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-209)

Rodríguez made his first direct contribution towards qualification, scoring a goal in a heated duel against Copa America champions Chile, securing a 1–1 away draw.[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-210) In early 2016, he provided both a goal and assist in a difficult away match against Bolivia resulting in a 2–3 victory.[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-211) Days later, he assisted another goal in a 3–1 home victory against Ecuador.[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-212) In early August, he contributed both a goal and an assist in Colombia's 2–0 victory against Venezuela.[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-213)

Starting off 2017, Rodríguez scored a late dramatic goal against a defensive Bolivia after missing an earlier penalty. The 1–0 home victory allowed Colombia to move to 4th place within the qualification group.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Days later, he scored and provided a goal in an impressive 0–2 victory in Ecuador.[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-214) For his first friendly of the year, Rodríguez assisted [Radamel Falcao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radamel_Falcao "Radamel Falcao")'s goal from the corner against European giants [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_national_football_team "Spanish national football team"). The game would end 2–2.[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-215) Days later against [Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameroonian_national_football_team "Cameroonian national football team"), Rodríguez both provided and scored a goal in a dominating 4–0 victory.[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-216) For the last qualification match of the 2018 World Cup, Rodríguez scored a crucial away goal against South American rival [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvian_national_football_team "Peruvian national football team"), resulting in a 1–1 draw and granting Colombia the last automatic qualification spot at fourth place.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] His last contribution of 2017 for Colombia would be an assist against [South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korean_national_football_team "South Korean national football team"), which ended 2–1.[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-217) Colombia's World Cup preparations in 2018 began against World Cup favorites [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_national_football_team "French national football team"), where Rodríguez provided two assists towards a comeback of a 2–0 score to a 2–3 victory. This marked the first victory in Colombia's history over France.[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-218)

#### 2018 World Cup, 2019 Copa América and 2021 Copa América

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e8/Poland_vs_Colombia_2018_World_Cup_11.jpg/250px-Poland_vs_Colombia_2018_World_Cup_11.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Poland_vs_Colombia_2018_World_Cup_11.jpg)

Rodríguez (front row, far right) with Colombia before [2018 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup "2018 FIFA World Cup") match against [Poland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poland_national_football_team "Poland national football team")

On 4 June 2018, Rodríguez was selected in Colombia's 23-man squad for the [2018 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup "2018 FIFA World Cup") in Russia.[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-219) He did not start in the opening game against [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan_national_football_team "Japan national football team") after a calf injury during training. He came as a substitute in the 59th minute for [Juan Quintero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Fernando_Quintero "Juan Fernando Quintero").[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-220) On 24 June 2018, he provided two assists in a 3–0 victory over [Poland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poland_national_football_team "Poland national football team") and was named as the Man of the Match.[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-221) Rodríguez had to be substituted in the 30th minute in the final match of the group stage against [Senegal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senegal_national_football_team "Senegal national football team") due to the injury.[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-222) He played in all three matches during the group phase, but was forced to sit out of Colombia's last 16 match against [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England_national_football_team "England national football team"). Colombia lost 4–3 on penalties against England and were eliminated from the World Cup. He was unable to score in those three matches.[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-223)

On 30 May 2019, Rodríguez was included in the 23-man final Colombia squad for the [2019 Copa América](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Copa_Am%C3%A9rica "2019 Copa América").[[224]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-224) In the quarter-finals of the tournament against defending champions Chile on 28 June, following a 0–0 draw after regulation time, he scored in the resulting penalty shoot-out; however, Colombia were defeated 5–4 and were eliminated from the competition.[[225]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-225) On 28 May 2021, Rodríguez was ruled out of the squad for the [2021 Copa América](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Am%C3%A9rica "2021 Copa América") due to his lack of conditioning, i.e. for not having the optimal physical level, as he had recently been recovering from injury.[[226]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-226)[[227]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-227)[[228]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-228)

#### 2022 World Cup qualification and 2024 Copa América

After Colombia's failure to qualify for the [2022 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup"), Rodríguez admitted that he was uncertain about his future with the team. "I don't know what's coming regarding the next phases, I don't know if I'm going to be there or not," he told _Diario Sport_. "What I do know is that it breaks my heart to lose, it bothers me not qualifying and this can't happen again."[[229]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-229) On 15 June 2024, Rodríguez earned his 100th international cap in a 3–0 friendly win over Bolivia.[[230]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-230) On 21 June, he was selected in the 26-man squad for the [2024 Copa América](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Copa_Am%C3%A9rica "2024 Copa América").[[231]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-231) In the quarter-final match against [Panama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panama_national_football_team "Panama national football team"), he scored a penalty and provided two assists in the first half of a 5–0 victory.[[232]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-232) In the semi-final clash against Uruguay, he provided the assist from a corner kick for [Jefferson Lerma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_Lerma "Jefferson Lerma")'s winner in a 1–0 victory to send his national team to the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Copa_Am%C3%A9rica_final "2024 Copa América final").[[233]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-233) This assist was his sixth at the tournament, which allowed Rodríguez to surpass Messi's record for the most assists in a single edition of Copa América.[[234]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-234)

#### 2026 World Cup and retirement

Rodríguez was selected in Colombia's 26-man squad for the [2026 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup "2026 FIFA World Cup"), becoming the eighth Colombian player to appear in three FIFA World Cup tournaments.[[235]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-235)[[236]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodriguez#cite_note-236) In Colombia's second group-stage match, he made his 10th World Cup appearance in a 1–0 victory over [DR Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DR_Congo_national_football_team "DR Congo national football team"), equaling the record for most World Cup appearances by a Colombian player, previously set by [Freddy Rincón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddy_Rinc%C3%B3n "Freddy Rincón") and [Carlos Valderrama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wi
