**Asamoah Gyan** ([/ˌ æ s ə ˈ m oʊ ə ˈ dʒ ɑː n/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_ASS-ə-MOH-ə JAHN_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key");[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-3) born 22 November 1985) is a Ghanaian former professional [footballer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") who played as a [striker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Striker_(association_football) "Striker (association football)"). He is a former [captain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_(association_football) "Captain (association football)") of the [Ghana national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_national_football_team "Ghana national football team").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-auto-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-6)

Gyan began his career in 2003 with [Ghana Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_Premier_League "Ghana Premier League") club [Liberty Professionals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_Professionals_F.C. "Liberty Professionals F.C."), scoring ten goals in sixteen matches. He then spent three seasons with [Serie. A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A") club [Udinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udinese_Calcio "Udinese Calcio") via two seasons [loan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loan_(sports) "Loan (sports)") at [Modena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modena_F.C. "Modena F.C."), netting on fifteen occasions in 53 league matches and at [Udinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udinese_Calcio "Udinese Calcio") where he scored 11 times in 39 league matches.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Asamoah_signs_Friuli_deal-7) In 2008, Gyan joined [Ligue 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ligue_1 "Ligue 1") club [Rennes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_Rennais_F.C. "Stade Rennais F.C."), netting fourteen times in forty-eight league matches during two seasons.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Rennes_:_Asamoah_Gyan_signe_4_ans-8) In 2010, Gyan joined then [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League") club [Sunderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunderland_A.F.C. "Sunderland A.F.C."), breaking the club's [transfer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transfer_window "Transfer window") record and netting on ten occasions in thirty-four Premier League matches during two seasons.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Asamoah_Gyan_joins_Sunderland_for_record_%C2%A313m_fee-9)

In 2011, Gyan joined [Al Ain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Ain_FC "Al Ain FC") of the [UAE Pro League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UAE_Pro_League "UAE Pro League") on loan and became the league's top goalscorer, scoring 22 times in 18 matches.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Gyan_deal_confirmed-10) In the following season, Gyan permanently joined Al Ain and helped them retain the Pro League title, once again, finishing as the league's top goalscorer with an impressive 31 goals in 22 matches.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Final_insult:_Sunderland_make_loss_on_Gyan_as_he_agrees_%C2%A3140k-a-week_move_after_tax.-11) In the [2013–14 league season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UAE_Pro_League "2013–14 UAE Pro League"), Gyan finished top scorer for a record third time, with 29 goals in 26 matches.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Asamoah_Gyan_inks_contract_extension_at_Al_Ain-12)

Gyan is the all-time leading goalscorer of the [Ghana national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_national_football_team "Ghana national football team"), with 51 goals.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-13) He represented Ghana at the [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup "2006 FIFA World Cup"), [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup "2010 FIFA World Cup") and [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup "2014 FIFA World Cup")[FIFA World Cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup"). With six goals, he is the top African goalscorer in the history of the World Cup. Gyan also represented Ghana at the [2004 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_tournament "Football at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament") and in seven [Africa Cup of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa_Cup_of_Nations "Africa Cup of Nations") ([2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2008 Africa Cup of Nations"), [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2010 Africa Cup of Nations"), [2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2012 Africa Cup of Nations"), [2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2013 Africa Cup of Nations"), [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2015 Africa Cup of Nations"), [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2017 Africa Cup of Nations") and [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2019 Africa Cup of Nations")), helping them finish in third place in 2008 and as runners-up in 2010 and 2015. He launched his memoir, titled "LeGYANdry" at the Kempinski Gold Coast Hotel in Accra.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-14) On 20 June 2023, Gyan announced his retirement from active football.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-15)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Gyan is the last born of his parents, Baffour Gyan Mensah (Father) and the late Madam Cecilia Amoako (Mother). His elder brother [Baffour Gyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baffour_Gyan "Baffour Gyan") is also a former professional footballer.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-16) Gyan was married to Gifty Sandra Dzamesi and together, they had three children, namely, Rafael Gyan, Frederick Gyan, Floyd Gyan.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-18)

## Club career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Club career")]

### Liberty Professionals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Liberty Professionals")]

Born in [Accra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accra "Accra"), Gyan had his early education at Seven Great Princess Academy in [Dansoman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dansoman "Dansoman") completing in 1999, and his secondary education at the [Accra Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accra_Academy "Accra Academy") from 1999 to 2002.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-19) Gyan started his career at Ghanaian club [Liberty Professionals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_Professionals_F.C. "Liberty Professionals F.C.") located in Accra. In his only top flight season with the club, he played 16 league matches in the [Ghana Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_Premier_League "Ghana Premier League") and scored 10 goals. He ended the season as the league's third top goal scorer.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-21)

### Udinese

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Udinese")]

Having signed for [Udinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udinese "Udinese") in 2003, he spent two years on [loan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loan_(sports) "Loan (sports)") at [Serie B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_B "Serie B") club [Modena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modena_F.C. "Modena F.C.") to gain match experience. Following some excellent displays during the [2006 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup "2006 FIFA World Cup"), he attracted interest from Russian club [Lokomotiv Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lokomotiv_Moscow "Lokomotiv Moscow"). Gyan returned to Udinese at the start of 2006, but on 17 February 2007, Udinese pulled out of a deal to sell him in the January [transfer window](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transfer_window "Transfer window"). The striker was on the verge of signing a three-year deal with Russian Club [Lokomotiv Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lokomotiv_Moscow "Lokomotiv Moscow") for [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")10.5 million, the fourth largest [transfer fee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transfer_(association_football) "Transfer (association football)") in Russian football history. "The striker Udinese targeted to replace me did not sign for them," Gyan told [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") Sport. "I've been told I will now have to stay in Italy for the rest of the season."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-22)

On 10 August 2007, along with [Fabio Quagliarella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabio_Quagliarella "Fabio Quagliarella"), Gyan signed an improved five-year contract extension to stay at Udinese until 30 June 2012, as a reward for his fine form[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-23) in the 2007–08 pre-season.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Asamoah_signs_Friuli_deal-7) "I have decided to stay here because it is one of the top leagues in the world," Asamoah said, "There is the possibility of me playing regular football here to make me a better player. "I am comfortable with the new deal and I know I can help Udinese achieve things for the future".[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-24) Gyan and Quagliarella marked their contract extensions with a brace each in Udinese's 7–0 friendly win later that evening.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Buon_pareggio-26)

On 29 July 2007, following his impressive [pre-season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preseason "Preseason") form, including a [hat-trick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hat-trick_(association_football) "Hat-trick (association football)")[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Buon_pareggio-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-27) in a [friendly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exhibition_game "Exhibition game") against [Serie B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_B "Serie B") outfit [Spezia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spezia_Calcio_1906 "Spezia Calcio 1906") on 25 July 2007, before Udinese sealed the long-term deal.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-29) Gyan scored eight goals in 2006–07 to help the Stadio Friuli club finish in 10th place in [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A").

Gyan was dogged by injury during the 2007–08 season and never appeared for Udinese again after January 2008, having played only 13 [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A") matches and scored 3 times that season.

### Rennes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Rennes")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/15/Asamoah_Gyan_Rennes_081231.jpg/250px-Asamoah_Gyan_Rennes_081231.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Asamoah_Gyan_Rennes_081231.jpg)

Gyan training whilst at Stade Rennais F.C.

On 11 July 2008, Gyan was signed by [Ligue 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ligue_1 "Ligue 1") club [Stade Rennais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_Rennais "Stade Rennais") for four years on an [€](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro "Euro")8 million transfer fee.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Rennes_:_Asamoah_Gyan_signe_4_ans-8)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-30) Gyan played 48 times for Rennes, scoring 14 goals. By the end of his stay at Rennes, he became well known for his goal scoring abilities, scoring 13 league goals in the 2009–10 season. However, Gyan only played three games in Ligue 1 the following season, taking his total appearances to 53, before he departed for Sunderland.

### Sunderland

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Sunderland")]

On 31 August 2010, Gyan signed for [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League") club [Sunderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunderland_A.F.C. "Sunderland A.F.C.") on a four-year deal for a club record £13 million.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Asamoah_Gyan_joins_Sunderland_for_record_%C2%A313m_fee-9) Gyan was later given the [squad number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squad_number_(association_football) "Squad number (association football)") 33 shirt at Sunderland. He scored on his Sunderland debut against [Wigan Athletic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wigan_Athletic_F.C. "Wigan Athletic F.C.") on 11 September after coming on as a [substitute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitute_(association_football) "Substitute (association football)") for [Danny Welbeck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Welbeck "Danny Welbeck"). The match ended in a 1–1 draw with [Antolín Alcaraz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antol%C3%ADn_Alcaraz "Antolín Alcaraz") scoring Wigan's equaliser.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-31) He marked his first start for Sunderland by netting their only goal in their [League Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_League_Cup "Football League Cup") exit at the hands of [West Ham United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Ham_United "West Ham United").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-32) Gyan scored twice on his first Premier League start for the club in a 2–0 win against [Stoke City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke_City_F.C. "Stoke City F.C.") on 6 November. His first [goal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scoring_in_association_football "Scoring in association football") came in the 9th minute when a [Nedum Onuoha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedum_Onuoha "Nedum Onuoha") shot was parried by goalkeeper [Asmir Begović](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asmir_Begovi%C4%87 "Asmir Begović"), with Gyan on hand to tap home the rebound and his second came in the 86th minute, to secure a 2–0 victory for the _Black Cats_.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-33) Three days later, he followed this up by scoring the equaliser against Tottenham at [White Hart Lane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Hart_Lane "White Hart Lane") in a 1–1 draw as Sunderland moved up to seventh in the table.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-34) He also scored a goal in Sunderland's 3–0 victory at [Stamford Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stamford_Bridge_(stadium) "Stamford Bridge (stadium)") against [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-35) Gyan scored Sunderland's third goal in their 3–0 victory over [Blackburn Rovers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackburn_Rovers_F.C. "Blackburn Rovers F.C.") on 1 January 2011.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-36)

On 16 January 2011, he started against local rivals [Newcastle United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newcastle_United_F.C. "Newcastle United F.C."), scoring a 94th-minute equaliser, preventing Newcastle gaining their second win of the season against Sunderland.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-37) Gyan added to his impressive goalscoring tally with a goal away at Stoke City on 5 February 2011. He scored an 11th-minute goal against Tottenham on 12 February 2011. Gyan's next goal came on 23 April as Sunderland beat [Wigan Athletic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wigan_Athletic_F.C. "Wigan Athletic F.C.") 4–2, a match which ended prematurely for the forward as he was [substituted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitute_(association_football) "Substitute (association football)") following a [hamstring injury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulled_hamstring "Pulled hamstring") which was expected to see him miss the remainder of the season.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-38) Gyan did recover in time to feature in Sunderland's last game of the season at West Ham but didn't add to his tally finishing his first season in English football with 10 league goals. Gyan took the [squad number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squad_number_(association_football) "Squad number (association football)") 3 shirt for the 2011–12 season, the same squad number he wore for Ghana.

### Al Ain

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Al Ain")]

On 10 September 2011, it was confirmed on the [Sunderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunderland_A.F.C. "Sunderland A.F.C.") website that Gyan would leave on a season long loan to club [Al Ain FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Ain_FC "Al Ain FC").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Gyan_deal_confirmed-10) Amid speculation of a fee of up to £6 million being paid for the [loan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loan_(sports) "Loan (sports)") period, with Gyan receiving up to four times his previous salary,[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-39) Chairman [Niall Quinn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niall_Quinn "Niall Quinn") emphasised the financial benefits of the deal for both Sunderland and the player. The Ghanaian finished the season with Al Ain by helping them capture their tenth league success and was the top goalscorer in the season with 22 league [goals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goal_(sport) "Goal (sport)").

When [Martin O'Neill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_O'Neill "Martin O'Neill") became manager of Sunderland on 8 December 2011, he considered the possibility of recalling Gyan from his loan spell away from the club.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-40)

Gyan [signed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signature "Signature") a five-year [contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football_contracts "Association football contracts") with Al Ain on 6 July 2012, worth over £6m per season.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Final_insult:_Sunderland_makes_a_loss_on_Gyan_as_he_agrees_%C2%A3140k-a-week_move_after_tax.-41) He was the top goalscorer in the UAE league in the 2013 season and helped his team retain the league title. On 24 July 2014, Gyan announced on his personal website that he had signed a contract extension at Al-Ain, receiving an improved deal and tying him to the club until 2018.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Asamoah_Gyan_inks_contract_extension_at_Al_Ain-12)

### Shanghai SIPG

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Shanghai SIPG")]

On 7 July 2015, Gyan confirmed on his own website that he had left [Al Ain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Ain_FC "Al Ain FC") and was set to join [Chinese Super League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Super_League "Chinese Super League") club [Shanghai SIPG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_SIPG_F.C. "Shanghai SIPG F.C."). Shanghai SIPG then officially announced they signed Gyan from Al Ain with an undisclosed fee.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Al_Ain_award_Asamoah_Gyan_for_dedicated_service_as_he_departs_to_China-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-43) It was then revealed that Gyan's weekly salary of £227,000 with his Chinese club instantly made him one of the world's best paid football players.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-44)

### Kayserispor

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Kayserispor")]

On 5 July 2017, he joined the Turkish club [Kayserispor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kayserispor "Kayserispor").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-45) On 9 August 2019, Gyan left Kayserispor.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-46)

### North East United

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: North East United")]

On 19 September 2019, he joined the Indian Super League side [NorthEast United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NorthEast_United_FC "NorthEast United FC").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-47) On 26 October 2019, he scored his first goal for Northeast United FC against [Odisha FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odisha_FC "Odisha FC") in the 84 th minute of the match as his team won the game by 2–1.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-48) Halfway through the season, he suffered an injury that would keep him out for the rest of the season, and on 15 January 2020, he was officially released from the club as Irish striker [Andy Keogh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Keogh "Andy Keogh") was signed as a replacement.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-49) He ended his time with Northeast United with a total of 4 goals in 8 appearances.

### Legon Cities

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Legon Cities")]

On 1 November 2020, Gyan returned to Ghana to join [Legon Cities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legon_Cities_FC "Legon Cities FC"),[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-50) in a loan deal worth more than 1 million dollars.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-51) He played his first match on 27 November 2020, coming on in the 71st minute for Raphael Ocloo in their goalless draw against [Medeama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medeama_S.C. "Medeama S.C."), marking a 17-year return to the [Ghana Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_Premier_League "Ghana Premier League") since leaving his boyhood club [Liberty Professionals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_Professionals_F.C. "Liberty Professionals F.C.") to sign for Italian club [Udinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udinese_Calcio "Udinese Calcio").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-52) On 3 June 2021, Gyan started his first match for the _Royals_ in the [2021 Ghanaian FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Ghanaian_FA_Cup "2021 Ghanaian FA Cup") Round of 64 match against [Uncle 'T'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncle_'T'_FC "Uncle 'T' FC"), which ended in a 2–1 victory at [Accra Sports Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accra_Sports_Stadium "Accra Sports Stadium") via a brace from [Richmond Antwi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond_Antwi "Richmond Antwi").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-54)

### Retirement

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Retirement")]

Gyan announced his retirement from active football on 20 June 2023, marking the end of a career spanning two decades.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-55) The announcement took place at the 30th Afreximbank Annual Meetings held at the [Accra International Conference Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accra_International_Conference_Centre "Accra International Conference Centre").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-:3-56)

Gyan's retirement statement reflected the sentiment that the time had come for him to bid farewell to his illustrious playing career, acknowledging the natural progression that all footballers eventually face.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-:3-56) He expressed gratitude to his country, family, colleagues, and everyone who contributed to his football journey. Gyan also expressed his intention to remain involved in the sport, focusing on coaching, football business, and scouting, while continuing to nurture young talents, as exemplified by his recent involvement in the Baby Jet U16 African Tournament.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-58)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-:3-56)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-59)

## International career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: International career")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b0/Asamoahgyan.jpg/250px-Asamoahgyan.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Asamoahgyan.jpg)

Gyan playing for Ghana in 2008

Gyan made his international debut at the age of 17, three days before his 18th birthday.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-:0-60) Gyan scored on his senior International debut for [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_national_football_team "Ghana national football team") against [Somalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somalia_national_football_team "Somalia national football team") on 19 November 2003, in the 90th minute.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-:1-61) He came on for [Nana Arhin Duah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nana_Arhin_Duah "Nana Arhin Duah") in the 77th minute in a [2006 FIFA World Cup qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification "2006 FIFA World Cup qualification"), three days before he turned 18 years; helping Ghana to win that game, and making him the youngest ever player to score for Ghana.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-:1-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-62)

He scored four times in seven matches during that successful World Cup qualifying campaign, helping Ghana to qualify for their first world cup in history. He was part of the [2004 Ghana Olympic squad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_team_squads#Ghana "Football at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's team squads"), who exited [in the first round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_tournament "Football at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament"), having finished in third place in [Group B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_tournament#Group_B "Football at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament").[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-:0-60)

He also scored the fastest [goal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goal_(sports) "Goal (sports)") of the tournament after 68 seconds. The strike was also Ghana's first ever goal in the [FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup"), coming in the [game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_E#Czech_Republic_vs_Ghana "2006 FIFA World Cup Group E") against the [Czech Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czech_Republic_national_football_team "Czech Republic national football team") on 17 June at the [RheinEnergieStadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RheinEnergieStadion "RheinEnergieStadion") in [Cologne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cologne "Cologne"), [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany"), which set the Black Stars on their way to a 2–0 victory.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-:2-63) He missed a penalty later in the game, and [received a yellow card](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup#Unprecedented_number_of_cards "2006 FIFA World Cup") ruling him out of the final group game for trying to take the penalty too early.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-:2-63) In Ghana's defeat to [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team") in the [round of 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Brazil_vs_Ghana "2006 FIFA World Cup knockout stage"), he was sent off in the 81st minute after collecting his second booking of the match (for [diving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diving_(association_football) "Diving (association football)")).[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-64)

On 24 January 2008, during the [Africa Cup of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2008 Africa Cup of Nations"), Gyan and his brother [Baffour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baffour_Gyan "Baffour Gyan") decided to walk out on the Black Stars following criticism after their unconvincing 1–0 win over [Namibia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_football_team "Namibia national football team").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-65) The media learnt the brothers had packed their bags and were ready to leave the team hotel but were persuaded to stay by teammates.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-66) In the [2010 Africa Cup of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2010 Africa Cup of Nations"), Asamoah Gyan helped a Ghana team, ravaged by injuries to the finals. Gyan scored three out of the four Ghana goals during the tournament.

Gyan scored with a penalty in the 85th minute of Ghana's first match of the [2010 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup "2010 FIFA World Cup") against [Serbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbia_national_football_team "Serbia national football team"), in a 1–0 win. He hit the [goalpost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_pitch#Goals "Football pitch") in the 92nd minute before being [substituted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitute_(association_football) "Substitute (association football)") to a standing ovation just before the final whistle.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-67) In Ghana's second game, he scored a penalty in the 26th minute to level the scores and earn his team a 1–1 draw against [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_men's_national_soccer_team "Australia men's national soccer team").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-68)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/Asamoah_Gyan_%26_Gary_Cahill_%28Ghana_vs._England%29.jpg/250px-Asamoah_Gyan_%26_Gary_Cahill_%28Ghana_vs._England%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Asamoah_Gyan_&_Gary_Cahill_(Ghana_vs._England).jpg)

Asamoah Gyan playing against England in 2011

In the round of 16 match against the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_men's_national_soccer_team "United States men's national soccer team"), he scored a goal in extra time allowing Ghana to win 2–1 and hence become the third African team in history to qualify to the tournament's quarter final, after [Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameroon_national_football_team "Cameroon national football team") and [Senegal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senegal_national_football_team "Senegal national football team").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-69) In the [quarter final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Uruguay_vs_Ghana "2010 FIFA World Cup knockout stage") tie against [Uruguay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uruguay_national_football_team "Uruguay national football team"), following [Luis Suárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Su%C3%A1rez "Luis Suárez")'s [handling of the ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fouls_and_misconduct_(association_football) "Fouls and misconduct (association football)") on the goal-line, he missed a [penalty kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_kick_(association_football) "Penalty kick (association football)") with no time remaining at end of [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports) "Overtime (sports)"), hitting the crossbar and necessitating a [penalty shootout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)") to decide the game. He converted his kick in the subsequent penalty shootout, but Uruguay went on to win the shootout 4–2.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-70)

For the second time in his career, Gyan missed a crucial penalty kick in a major tournament when he had his penalty kick saved in the [2012 African Cup of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2012 Africa Cup of Nations") semi-final. Ghana went on to lose 1–0. After missing that penalty kick, Gyan decided to take an "indefinite break" from international football.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-71) On 8 May 2012, he announced his return to the Black Stars team.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-73)

On 7 June 2013, he scored 2 goals in a 3–1 win over [Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan_national_football_team "Sudan national football team") in a World Cup qualifier to make him the country's leading goalscorer, surpassing [Abedi Pele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abedi_Pele "Abedi Pele")'s 33 goals.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-74)

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/Gyan_AfCON_2015.jpg/250px-Gyan_AfCON_2015.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Gyan_AfCON_2015.jpg)

Gyan playing for Ghana at the AFCON 2015

On 2 June 2014, Gyan was named in [Ghana's squad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup_squads#Ghana "2014 FIFA World Cup squads") for the [2014 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup "2014 FIFA World Cup").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-75) In the team's opening match, he [captained](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_(association_football) "Captain (association football)") the Black Stars against the United States in a 2–1 defeat.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-76) He scored his first goal of the tournament in a 2–2 draw with [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany_national_football_team "Germany national football team"),[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-77) equaling [Roger Milla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Milla "Roger Milla")'s record of five [FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup") goals. In the final group match, he became the top African goalscorer in World Cup finals history by scoring the Black Stars' goal as they were defeated 2–1 by [Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portugal_national_football_team "Portugal national football team").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-78)

At the [2015 Africa Cup of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2015 Africa Cup of Nations"), Gyan missed Ghana's opening match, a 2–1 loss to Senegal, with a "mild bout" of malaria.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-79) He returned for the second match, scoring a last minute winning goal against the tournament favourite [Algeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algeria_national_football_team "Algeria national football team") in a 1–0 win for the Black Stars.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-80) An international exile lasting over a year was ended in October 2018 when Gyan was called up to the Ghanaian squad for a pair of [2019 Africa Cup of Nations qualification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Africa_Cup_of_Nations_qualification "2019 Africa Cup of Nations qualification") matches versus [Sierra Leone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Leone_national_football_team "Sierra Leone national football team").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-81)

He announced his retirement from international football on 20 May 2019, a month to the 2019 Africa Cup of Nations.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-82) However, a day later Gyan reversed his decision following a discussion with the president of Ghana, [Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nana_Akufo-Addo "Nana Akufo-Addo").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-83)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-auto-4)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-84)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-85) In early August 2022 Gyan released a statement that he was training to get back to full fitness to play in the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-86) Gyan was not part of the 26 man squad selected to represent Ghana in the World Cup 2022 and since then has been an ample supporter of the Black Stars and has been leading fan festivals and ceremonies.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-87) Gyan retired as Ghana's all-time leading goal scorer, amassing a total of 51 goals in 109 appearances for his country. He also retires holding the record for the highest number of goals scored by any African player in the history of the [World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup"), with a tally of six goals.

**Asamoah Gyan** ([/ˌ æ s ə ˈ m oʊ ə ˈ dʒ ɑː n/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_ASS-ə-MOH-ə JAHN_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key");[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-3) born 22 November 1985) is a Ghanaian former professional [footballer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") who played as a [striker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Striker_(association_football) "Striker (association football)"). He is a former [captain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_(association_football) "Captain (association football)") of the [Ghana national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_national_football_team "Ghana national football team").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-auto-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-6)

Gyan began his career in 2003 with [Ghana Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_Premier_League "Ghana Premier League") club [Liberty Professionals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_Professionals_F.C. "Liberty Professionals F.C."), scoring ten goals in sixteen matches. He then spent three seasons with [Serie. A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A") club [Udinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udinese_Calcio "Udinese Calcio") via two seasons [loan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loan_(sports) "Loan (sports)") at [Modena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modena_F.C. "Modena F.C."), netting on fifteen occasions in 53 league matches and at [Udinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udinese_Calcio "Udinese Calcio") where he scored 11 times in 39 league matches.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Asamoah_signs_Friuli_deal-7) In 2008, Gyan joined [Ligue 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ligue_1 "Ligue 1") club [Rennes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_Rennais_F.C. "Stade Rennais F.C."), netting fourteen times in forty-eight league matches during two seasons.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Rennes_:_Asamoah_Gyan_signe_4_ans-8) In 2010, Gyan joined then [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League") club [Sunderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunderland_A.F.C. "Sunderland A.F.C."), breaking the club's [transfer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transfer_window "Transfer window") record and netting on ten occasions in thirty-four Premier League matches during two seasons.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Asamoah_Gyan_joins_Sunderland_for_record_%C2%A313m_fee-9)

In 2011, Gyan joined [Al Ain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Ain_FC "Al Ain FC") of the [UAE Pro League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UAE_Pro_League "UAE Pro League") on loan and became the league's top goalscorer, scoring 22 times in 18 matches.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Gyan_deal_confirmed-10) In the following season, Gyan permanently joined Al Ain and helped them retain the Pro League title, once again, finishing as the league's top goalscorer with an impressive 31 goals in 22 matches.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Final_insult:_Sunderland_make_loss_on_Gyan_as_he_agrees_%C2%A3140k-a-week_move_after_tax.-11) In the [2013–14 league season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UAE_Pro_League "2013–14 UAE Pro League"), Gyan finished top scorer for a record third time, with 29 goals in 26 matches.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Asamoah_Gyan_inks_contract_extension_at_Al_Ain-12)

Gyan is the all-time leading goalscorer of the [Ghana national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_national_football_team "Ghana national football team"), with 51 goals.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-13) He represented Ghana at the [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup "2006 FIFA World Cup"), [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup "2010 FIFA World Cup") and [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup "2014 FIFA World Cup")[FIFA World Cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup"). With six goals, he is the top African goalscorer in the history of the World Cup. Gyan also represented Ghana at the [2004 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_tournament "Football at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament") and in seven [Africa Cup of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa_Cup_of_Nations "Africa Cup of Nations") ([2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2008 Africa Cup of Nations"), [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2010 Africa Cup of Nations"), [2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2012 Africa Cup of Nations"), [2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2013 Africa Cup of Nations"), [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2015 Africa Cup of Nations"), [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2017 Africa Cup of Nations") and [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2019 Africa Cup of Nations")), helping them finish in third place in 2008 and as runners-up in 2010 and 2015. He launched his memoir, titled "LeGYANdry" at the Kempinski Gold Coast Hotel in Accra.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-14) On 20 June 2023, Gyan announced his retirement from active football.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-15)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Gyan is the last born of his parents, Baffour Gyan Mensah (Father) and the late Madam Cecilia Amoako (Mother). His elder brother [Baffour Gyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baffour_Gyan "Baffour Gyan") is also a former professional footballer.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-16) Gyan was married to Gifty Sandra Dzamesi and together, they had three children, namely, Rafael Gyan, Frederick Gyan, Floyd Gyan.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-18)

## Club career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Club career")]

### Liberty Professionals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Liberty Professionals")]

Born in [Accra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accra "Accra"), Gyan had his early education at Seven Great Princess Academy in [Dansoman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dansoman "Dansoman") completing in 1999, and his secondary education at the [Accra Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accra_Academy "Accra Academy") from 1999 to 2002.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-19) Gyan started his career at Ghanaian club [Liberty Professionals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_Professionals_F.C. "Liberty Professionals F.C.") located in Accra. In his only top flight season with the club, he played 16 league matches in the [Ghana Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_Premier_League "Ghana Premier League") and scored 10 goals. He ended the season as the league's third top goal scorer.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-21)

### Udinese

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Udinese")]

Having signed for [Udinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udinese "Udinese") in 2003, he spent two years on [loan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loan_(sports) "Loan (sports)") at [Serie B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_B "Serie B") club [Modena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modena_F.C. "Modena F.C.") to gain match experience. Following some excellent displays during the [2006 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup "2006 FIFA World Cup"), he attracted interest from Russian club [Lokomotiv Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lokomotiv_Moscow "Lokomotiv Moscow"). Gyan returned to Udinese at the start of 2006, but on 17 February 2007, Udinese pulled out of a deal to sell him in the January [transfer window](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transfer_window "Transfer window"). The striker was on the verge of signing a three-year deal with Russian Club [Lokomotiv Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lokomotiv_Moscow "Lokomotiv Moscow") for [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")10.5 million, the fourth largest [transfer fee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transfer_(association_football) "Transfer (association football)") in Russian football history. "The striker Udinese targeted to replace me did not sign for them," Gyan told [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") Sport. "I've been told I will now have to stay in Italy for the rest of the season."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-22)

On 10 August 2007, along with [Fabio Quagliarella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabio_Quagliarella "Fabio Quagliarella"), Gyan signed an improved five-year contract extension to stay at Udinese until 30 June 2012, as a reward for his fine form[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-23) in the 2007–08 pre-season.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Asamoah_signs_Friuli_deal-7) "I have decided to stay here because it is one of the top leagues in the world," Asamoah said, "There is the possibility of me playing regular football here to make me a better player. "I am comfortable with the new deal and I know I can help Udinese achieve things for the future".[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-24) Gyan and Quagliarella marked their contract extensions with a brace each in Udinese's 7–0 friendly win later that evening.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Buon_pareggio-26)

On 29 July 2007, following his impressive [pre-season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preseason "Preseason") form, including a [hat-trick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hat-trick_(association_football) "Hat-trick (association football)")[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Buon_pareggio-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-27) in a [friendly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exhibition_game "Exhibition game") against [Serie B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_B "Serie B") outfit [Spezia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spezia_Calcio_1906 "Spezia Calcio 1906") on 25 July 2007, before Udinese sealed the long-term deal.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-29) Gyan scored eight goals in 2006–07 to help the Stadio Friuli club finish in 10th place in [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A").

Gyan was dogged by injury during the 2007–08 season and never appeared for Udinese again after January 2008, having played only 13 [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A") matches and scored 3 times that season.

### Rennes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Rennes")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/15/Asamoah_Gyan_Rennes_081231.jpg/250px-Asamoah_Gyan_Rennes_081231.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Asamoah_Gyan_Rennes_081231.jpg)

Gyan training whilst at Stade Rennais F.C.

On 11 July 2008, Gyan was signed by [Ligue 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ligue_1 "Ligue 1") club [Stade Rennais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_Rennais "Stade Rennais") for four years on an [€](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro "Euro")8 million transfer fee.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Rennes_:_Asamoah_Gyan_signe_4_ans-8)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-30) Gyan played 48 times for Rennes, scoring 14 goals. By the end of his stay at Rennes, he became well known for his goal scoring abilities, scoring 13 league goals in the 2009–10 season. However, Gyan only played three games in Ligue 1 the following season, taking his total appearances to 53, before he departed for Sunderland.

### Sunderland

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Sunderland")]

On 31 August 2010, Gyan signed for [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League") club [Sunderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunderland_A.F.C. "Sunderland A.F.C.") on a four-year deal for a club record £13 million.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Asamoah_Gyan_joins_Sunderland_for_record_%C2%A313m_fee-9) Gyan was later given the [squad number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squad_number_(association_football) "Squad number (association football)") 33 shirt at Sunderland. He scored on his Sunderland debut against [Wigan Athletic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wigan_Athletic_F.C. "Wigan Athletic F.C.") on 11 September after coming on as a [substitute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitute_(association_football) "Substitute (association football)") for [Danny Welbeck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Welbeck "Danny Welbeck"). The match ended in a 1–1 draw with [Antolín Alcaraz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antol%C3%ADn_Alcaraz "Antolín Alcaraz") scoring Wigan's equaliser.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-31) He marked his first start for Sunderland by netting their only goal in their [League Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_League_Cup "Football League Cup") exit at the hands of [West Ham United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Ham_United "West Ham United").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-32) Gyan scored twice on his first Premier League start for the club in a 2–0 win against [Stoke City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke_City_F.C. "Stoke City F.C.") on 6 November. His first [goal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scoring_in_association_football "Scoring in association football") came in the 9th minute when a [Nedum Onuoha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedum_Onuoha "Nedum Onuoha") shot was parried by goalkeeper [Asmir Begović](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asmir_Begovi%C4%87 "Asmir Begović"), with Gyan on hand to tap home the rebound and his second came in the 86th minute, to secure a 2–0 victory for the _Black Cats_.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-33) Three days later, he followed this up by scoring the equaliser against Tottenham at [White Hart Lane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Hart_Lane "White Hart Lane") in a 1–1 draw as Sunderland moved up to seventh in the table.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-34) He also scored a goal in Sunderland's 3–0 victory at [Stamford Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stamford_Bridge_(stadium) "Stamford Bridge (stadium)") against [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-35) Gyan scored Sunderland's third goal in their 3–0 victory over [Blackburn Rovers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackburn_Rovers_F.C. "Blackburn Rovers F.C.") on 1 January 2011.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-36)

On 16 January 2011, he started against local rivals [Newcastle United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newcastle_United_F.C. "Newcastle United F.C."), scoring a 94th-minute equaliser, preventing Newcastle gaining their second win of the season against Sunderland.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-37) Gyan added to his impressive goalscoring tally with a goal away at Stoke City on 5 February 2011. He scored an 11th-minute goal against Tottenham on 12 February 2011. Gyan's next goal came on 23 April as Sunderland beat [Wigan Athletic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wigan_Athletic_F.C. "Wigan Athletic F.C.") 4–2, a match which ended prematurely for the forward as he was [substituted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitute_(association_football) "Substitute (association football)") following a [hamstring injury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulled_hamstring "Pulled hamstring") which was expected to see him miss the remainder of the season.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-38) Gyan did recover in time to feature in Sunderland's last game of the season at West Ham but didn't add to his tally finishing his first season in English football with 10 league goals. Gyan took the [squad number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squad_number_(association_football) "Squad number (association football)") 3 shirt for the 2011–12 season, the same squad number he wore for Ghana.

### Al Ain

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Al Ain")]

On 10 September 2011, it was confirmed on the [Sunderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunderland_A.F.C. "Sunderland A.F.C.") website that Gyan would leave on a season long loan to club [Al Ain FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Ain_FC "Al Ain FC").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Gyan_deal_confirmed-10) Amid speculation of a fee of up to £6 million being paid for the [loan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loan_(sports) "Loan (sports)") period, with Gyan receiving up to four times his previous salary,[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-39) Chairman [Niall Quinn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niall_Quinn "Niall Quinn") emphasised the financial benefits of the deal for both Sunderland and the player. The Ghanaian finished the season with Al Ain by helping them capture their tenth league success and was the top goalscorer in the season with 22 league [goals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goal_(sport) "Goal (sport)").

When [Martin O'Neill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_O'Neill "Martin O'Neill") became manager of Sunderland on 8 December 2011, he considered the possibility of recalling Gyan from his loan spell away from the club.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-40)

Gyan [signed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signature "Signature") a five-year [contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football_contracts "Association football contracts") with Al Ain on 6 July 2012, worth over £6m per season.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Final_insult:_Sunderland_makes_a_loss_on_Gyan_as_he_agrees_%C2%A3140k-a-week_move_after_tax.-41) He was the top goalscorer in the UAE league in the 2013 season and helped his team retain the league title. On 24 July 2014, Gyan announced on his personal website that he had signed a contract extension at Al-Ain, receiving an improved deal and tying him to the club until 2018.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Asamoah_Gyan_inks_contract_extension_at_Al_Ain-12)

### Shanghai SIPG

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Shanghai SIPG")]

On 7 July 2015, Gyan confirmed on his own website that he had left [Al Ain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Ain_FC "Al Ain FC") and was set to join [Chinese Super League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Super_League "Chinese Super League") club [Shanghai SIPG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_SIPG_F.C. "Shanghai SIPG F.C."). Shanghai SIPG then officially announced they signed Gyan from Al Ain with an undisclosed fee.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-Al_Ain_award_Asamoah_Gyan_for_dedicated_service_as_he_departs_to_China-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-43) It was then revealed that Gyan's weekly salary of £227,000 with his Chinese club instantly made him one of the world's best paid football players.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-44)

### Kayserispor

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Kayserispor")]

On 5 July 2017, he joined the Turkish club [Kayserispor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kayserispor "Kayserispor").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-45) On 9 August 2019, Gyan left Kayserispor.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-46)

### North East United

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: North East United")]

On 19 September 2019, he joined the Indian Super League side [NorthEast United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NorthEast_United_FC "NorthEast United FC").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-47) On 26 October 2019, he scored his first goal for Northeast United FC against [Odisha FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odisha_FC "Odisha FC") in the 84 th minute of the match as his team won the game by 2–1.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-48) Halfway through the season, he suffered an injury that would keep him out for the rest of the season, and on 15 January 2020, he was officially released from the club as Irish striker [Andy Keogh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Keogh "Andy Keogh") was signed as a replacement.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-49) He ended his time with Northeast United with a total of 4 goals in 8 appearances.

### Legon Cities

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Legon Cities")]

On 1 November 2020, Gyan returned to Ghana to join [Legon Cities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legon_Cities_FC "Legon Cities FC"),[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-50) in a loan deal worth more than 1 million dollars.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-51) He played his first match on 27 November 2020, coming on in the 71st minute for Raphael Ocloo in their goalless draw against [Medeama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medeama_S.C. "Medeama S.C."), marking a 17-year return to the [Ghana Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_Premier_League "Ghana Premier League") since leaving his boyhood club [Liberty Professionals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_Professionals_F.C. "Liberty Professionals F.C.") to sign for Italian club [Udinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udinese_Calcio "Udinese Calcio").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-52) On 3 June 2021, Gyan started his first match for the _Royals_ in the [2021 Ghanaian FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Ghanaian_FA_Cup "2021 Ghanaian FA Cup") Round of 64 match against [Uncle 'T'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncle_'T'_FC "Uncle 'T' FC"), which ended in a 2–1 victory at [Accra Sports Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accra_Sports_Stadium "Accra Sports Stadium") via a brace from [Richmond Antwi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond_Antwi "Richmond Antwi").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-54)

### Retirement

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Retirement")]

Gyan announced his retirement from active football on 20 June 2023, marking the end of a career spanning two decades.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-55) The announcement took place at the 30th Afreximbank Annual Meetings held at the [Accra International Conference Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accra_International_Conference_Centre "Accra International Conference Centre").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-:3-56)

Gyan's retirement statement reflected the sentiment that the time had come for him to bid farewell to his illustrious playing career, acknowledging the natural progression that all footballers eventually face.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-:3-56) He expressed gratitude to his country, family, colleagues, and everyone who contributed to his football journey. Gyan also expressed his intention to remain involved in the sport, focusing on coaching, football business, and scouting, while continuing to nurture young talents, as exemplified by his recent involvement in the Baby Jet U16 African Tournament.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-58)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-:3-56)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-59)

## International career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Asamoah_Gyan&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: International career")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b0/Asamoahgyan.jpg/250px-Asamoahgyan.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Asamoahgyan.jpg)

Gyan playing for Ghana in 2008

Gyan made his international debut at the age of 17, three days before his 18th birthday.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-:0-60) Gyan scored on his senior International debut for [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_national_football_team "Ghana national football team") against [Somalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somalia_national_football_team "Somalia national football team") on 19 November 2003, in the 90th minute.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-:1-61) He came on for [Nana Arhin Duah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nana_Arhin_Duah "Nana Arhin Duah") in the 77th minute in a [2006 FIFA World Cup qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification "2006 FIFA World Cup qualification"), three days before he turned 18 years; helping Ghana to win that game, and making him the youngest ever player to score for Ghana.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-:1-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-62)

He scored four times in seven matches during that successful World Cup qualifying campaign, helping Ghana to qualify for their first world cup in history. He was part of the [2004 Ghana Olympic squad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_team_squads#Ghana "Football at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's team squads"), who exited [in the first round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_tournament "Football at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament"), having finished in third place in [Group B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_tournament#Group_B "Football at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament").[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-:0-60)

He also scored the fastest [goal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goal_(sports) "Goal (sports)") of the tournament after 68 seconds. The strike was also Ghana's first ever goal in the [FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup"), coming in the [game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_E#Czech_Republic_vs_Ghana "2006 FIFA World Cup Group E") against the [Czech Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czech_Republic_national_football_team "Czech Republic national football team") on 17 June at the [RheinEnergieStadion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RheinEnergieStadion "RheinEnergieStadion") in [Cologne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cologne "Cologne"), [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany"), which set the Black Stars on their way to a 2–0 victory.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-:2-63) He missed a penalty later in the game, and [received a yellow card](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup#Unprecedented_number_of_cards "2006 FIFA World Cup") ruling him out of the final group game for trying to take the penalty too early.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-:2-63) In Ghana's defeat to [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team") in the [round of 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Brazil_vs_Ghana "2006 FIFA World Cup knockout stage"), he was sent off in the 81st minute after collecting his second booking of the match (for [diving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diving_(association_football) "Diving (association football)")).[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-64)

On 24 January 2008, during the [Africa Cup of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2008 Africa Cup of Nations"), Gyan and his brother [Baffour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baffour_Gyan "Baffour Gyan") decided to walk out on the Black Stars following criticism after their unconvincing 1–0 win over [Namibia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_national_football_team "Namibia national football team").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-65) The media learnt the brothers had packed their bags and were ready to leave the team hotel but were persuaded to stay by teammates.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-66) In the [2010 Africa Cup of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2010 Africa Cup of Nations"), Asamoah Gyan helped a Ghana team, ravaged by injuries to the finals. Gyan scored three out of the four Ghana goals during the tournament.

Gyan scored with a penalty in the 85th minute of Ghana's first match of the [2010 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup "2010 FIFA World Cup") against [Serbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbia_national_football_team "Serbia national football team"), in a 1–0 win. He hit the [goalpost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_pitch#Goals "Football pitch") in the 92nd minute before being [substituted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitute_(association_football) "Substitute (association football)") to a standing ovation just before the final whistle.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-67) In Ghana's second game, he scored a penalty in the 26th minute to level the scores and earn his team a 1–1 draw against [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_men's_national_soccer_team "Australia men's national soccer team").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-68)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/Asamoah_Gyan_%26_Gary_Cahill_%28Ghana_vs._England%29.jpg/250px-Asamoah_Gyan_%26_Gary_Cahill_%28Ghana_vs._England%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Asamoah_Gyan_&_Gary_Cahill_(Ghana_vs._England).jpg)

Asamoah Gyan playing against England in 2011

In the round of 16 match against the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_men's_national_soccer_team "United States men's national soccer team"), he scored a goal in extra time allowing Ghana to win 2–1 and hence become the third African team in history to qualify to the tournament's quarter final, after [Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameroon_national_football_team "Cameroon national football team") and [Senegal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senegal_national_football_team "Senegal national football team").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-69) In the [quarter final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Uruguay_vs_Ghana "2010 FIFA World Cup knockout stage") tie against [Uruguay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uruguay_national_football_team "Uruguay national football team"), following [Luis Suárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Su%C3%A1rez "Luis Suárez")'s [handling of the ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fouls_and_misconduct_(association_football) "Fouls and misconduct (association football)") on the goal-line, he missed a [penalty kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_kick_(association_football) "Penalty kick (association football)") with no time remaining at end of [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports) "Overtime (sports)"), hitting the crossbar and necessitating a [penalty shootout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)") to decide the game. He converted his kick in the subsequent penalty shootout, but Uruguay went on to win the shootout 4–2.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-70)

For the second time in his career, Gyan missed a crucial penalty kick in a major tournament when he had his penalty kick saved in the [2012 African Cup of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2012 Africa Cup of Nations") semi-final. Ghana went on to lose 1–0. After missing that penalty kick, Gyan decided to take an "indefinite break" from international football.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-71) On 8 May 2012, he announced his return to the Black Stars team.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-73)

On 7 June 2013, he scored 2 goals in a 3–1 win over [Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan_national_football_team "Sudan national football team") in a World Cup qualifier to make him the country's leading goalscorer, surpassing [Abedi Pele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abedi_Pele "Abedi Pele")'s 33 goals.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-74)

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/Gyan_AfCON_2015.jpg/250px-Gyan_AfCON_2015.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Gyan_AfCON_2015.jpg)

Gyan playing for Ghana at the AFCON 2015

On 2 June 2014, Gyan was named in [Ghana's squad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup_squads#Ghana "2014 FIFA World Cup squads") for the [2014 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup "2014 FIFA World Cup").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-75) In the team's opening match, he [captained](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_(association_football) "Captain (association football)") the Black Stars against the United States in a 2–1 defeat.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-76) He scored his first goal of the tournament in a 2–2 draw with [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany_national_football_team "Germany national football team"),[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-77) equaling [Roger Milla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Milla "Roger Milla")'s record of five [FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup") goals. In the final group match, he became the top African goalscorer in World Cup finals history by scoring the Black Stars' goal as they were defeated 2–1 by [Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portugal_national_football_team "Portugal national football team").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-78)

At the [2015 Africa Cup of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2015 Africa Cup of Nations"), Gyan missed Ghana's opening match, a 2–1 loss to Senegal, with a "mild bout" of malaria.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-79) He returned for the second match, scoring a last minute winning goal against the tournament favourite [Algeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algeria_national_football_team "Algeria national football team") in a 1–0 win for the Black Stars.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-80) An international exile lasting over a year was ended in October 2018 when Gyan was called up to the Ghanaian squad for a pair of [2019 Africa Cup of Nations qualification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Africa_Cup_of_Nations_qualification "2019 Africa Cup of Nations qualification") matches versus [Sierra Leone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Leone_national_football_team "Sierra Leone national football team").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-81)

He announced his retirement from international football on 20 May 2019, a month to the 2019 Africa Cup of Nations.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-82) However, a day later Gyan reversed his decision following a discussion with the president of Ghana, [Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nana_Akufo-Addo "Nana Akufo-Addo").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-83)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-auto-4)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-84)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-85) In early August 2022 Gyan released a statement that he was training to get back to full fitness to play in the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-86) Gyan was not part of the 26 man squad selected to represent Ghana in the World Cup 2022 and since then has been an ample supporter of the Black Stars and has been leading fan festivals and ceremonies.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asamoah_Gyan#cite_note-87) Gyan retired as Ghana's all-time leading goal scorer, amassing a total of 51 goals in 109 appearances for his country. He also retires holding the record for the highest number of goals scored by any African player in the history of the [World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup"), with a tally of six goals.
